headline: Samsung and SK hynix both showed next-generation HBM4E AI memory at Seoul's SEDEX 2026 chip show, along with rival ideas to ease memory bottlenecks.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: trade-show product reveals, with the newest ideas still at concept stage.
importance_line: It affects AI chip buyers such as Nvidia and the memory makers' investors, and the specifications are company claims while zHBM and flash-based ideas are still concepts.
summary: Chosunbiz reports that Samsung Electronics and SK hynix unveiled HBM4E, the next generation of high-bandwidth memory (stacked memory chips that sit beside AI processors), at SEDEX 2026 in Seoul, with Samsung quoting 14 to 16 gigabits per second per pin, more than 20% faster than HBM4, and SK hynix quoting over 20% better energy efficiency. Samsung also showed zHBM, which stacks memory on top of the processor, and SK hynix showed high-bandwidth flash, which it expects to hold about 10 times the capacity of HBM; Chosunbiz notes both are still at concept or development stage.
